macro_context.market_sentiment: Risk-off on May 4, 2026: Dow -1.13% (-557pts to 48,941), S&P 500 -0.41% to 7,200.75, Nasdaq -0.19% to 25,067.80. UAE intercepted Iranian missiles (first activation since US-Iran ceasefire), oil surged, 10-yr Treasury yield rose to 4.45%. Prior week (May 1) saw record closes for Nasdaq and S&P 500.
macro_context.fed_outlook: Fed held rates steady at 3.5%-3.75% on April 29, 2026 in an unusual 8-4 split vote (first 4-member dissent since Oct 1992). Powell may have chaired his final meeting; markets pricing zero rate changes for remainder of 2026 and first cut not until Dec 2027. Fed cited elevated inflation from global energy prices and Middle East conflict uncertainty.
macro_context.geopolitical: Iran-UAE missile exchange on May 4 escalated Middle East conflict; Israel and Bahrain on high alert. Strait of Hormuz closure risk raised by IMF. US also intervening in Venezuela. These risks layer onto existing tariff uncertainty and a pending Fed leadership change, pushing oil higher and weighing on risk assets.

analyst_consensus.recent_changes: Strong post-earnings upgrade wave on May 1, 2026: Mizuho to $470, Goldman Sachs to $400, TD Cowen to $500, BofA to $572, Wedbush and JP Morgan maintained ~$530. 25-analyst consensus: Strong Buy (20 Strong Buy, 1 Moderate Buy, 4 Hold). No recent downgrades. 12-month target range $285-$660 across 18-23 analyst coverage groups. Morgan Stanley has Overweight. (Sources: StockAnalysis, MarketBeat, Benzinga, TickerNerd)

web_context.competitor_activity: WDC and Seagate form an HDD duopoly (>85% global share); competition has shifted from price to who can scale 40TB+ HAMR drives fastest — both report 2026 HDD capacity fully committed. WDC has a slight share edge (~45% vs Seagate ~42%). Post-SanDisk-spin-off ($3.1B final stake sold Feb 2026), WDC is a pure-play HDD/AI-storage company. Both WDC and Seagate benefit from a global NAND shortage (memory makers diverting capacity to HBM for AI), driving enterprise SSD price hikes 30-60%. Micron's blowout DRAM/HBM results in March 2026 further validated the AI storage supercycle thesis. (Sources: Yahoo Finance, FinancialContent, MarketBeat)
web_context.earnings_info: Q3 FY2026 reported April 30, 2026 (after close): Revenue $3.0B, EPS $5.27 — beat estimates by ~$313M at midpoint. Q4 FY2026 guidance: Revenue $3.65B +/- $100M (~40% YoY growth at midpoint), gross margin 51-52%. Next earnings (Q4 FY2026) scheduled August 5, 2026 after close (confirmed). Analyst EPS estimate for Q4: ~$3.21. (Sources: MarketBeat, WesternDigital.com press release, Motley Fool transcript)
